core_obligations: Introduce the boundary maps (proof lines 4813-4825): the author defines the maps whose images control the quotients of the inverse system, and shows that the direct sum of the images is a graded submodule of the direct sum of the target cohomology groups, using the graded compatibility of the boundary maps.

Use finite generation (proof lines 4825-4845): by the ascending chain condition the author chooses finitely many homogeneous generators and lets c be their maximum, so that beyond c every element of the system is corrected by a combination of the generators.

Conclude the stable image (proof lines 4845-4862): the correction lifts to the next stage and the combination dies further down, which gives the equality of images required for the Mittag-Leffler condition in the stable form.
proof_roadmap: Define the boundary maps of the short exact sequences and check the graded compatibility.
Use finite generation of the graded module of their images to choose finitely many generators.
Correct an arbitrary element by a combination of generators to lift it, which gives the stable image.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the sharper form of the Mittag-Leffler criterion for the cohomology of an inverse system of sheaves on a site: the hypothesis is now the ascending chain condition on the graded module of the stable images of the boundary maps N_n, and the conclusion is the Mittag-Leffler condition in its stable-image form (statement lines 4788-4811). The proof introduces the boundary maps and verifies that the direct sum of their images is a graded submodule using the graded compatibility (proof lines 4813-4825), extracts finitely many homogeneous generators from the chain condition and chooses their maximum level (proof lines 4825-4845), and then corrects an arbitrary element by a combination of the generators so that it lifts, which yields the stable image (proof lines 4845-4862). The non-formal content is the passage from finite generation to the stable-image statement. The claim is H2: the same architecture as its companion, with the sharper hypothesis used in the same place.
